Posting Title

(Associate/Undergraduate) Intern - Carbon Management and Large Energy Systems

.

Location

Remote

.

Position Type

Intern (Fixed Term)

.

Hours Per Week

20

.

Working at NLR

Join the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR), where world-class scientists, engineers, and experts are accelerating energy innovation through breakthrough research and systems integration. From our mission to our collaborative culture, NLR stands out in the research community for its commitment to an affordable and secure energy future. Spanning foundational science to applied systems engineering and analysis, we focus on solving complex challenges to deliver advanced, secure, reliable, and cost-effective energy solutions. Our work helps strengthen U.S. industries, support job creation, and promote national economic growth.

At NLR, you'll find a mission-driven environment supported by state-of-the-art facilities, multidisciplinary research teams, and strong collaborations with industry, academia, and other national laboratories. We offer robust professional development opportunities, and a competitive benefits package designed to support your career and well-being.

Job Description

The National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) is seeking two student interns to support its collaboration with the Kern Community College District’s California Renewable Energy Laboratory (CREL).

Interns will work with researchers in the Strategic Energy Analysis Center on applied research and educational activities related to carbon management, bio-based products, industrial energy systems, and large energy-load systems. The Strategic Energy Analysis Center (SEAC; www.nlr.gov/analysis) aims to increase understanding of energy policies, markets, resources, technologies, and infrastructure to address U.S. economic, security, and environmental priorities.

The two positions may support different combinations of research analysis, education, and curriculum-development activities. Specific project scopes will be determined in collaboration with the assigned NLR researchers based on project needs and the interns’ backgrounds and interests. Examples of potential work areas include:

Work Areas

- Biomass-derived intermediates and bio-based chemicals
- Carbon efficiency of bio-based conversion pathways
- Carbon utilization and low-carbon industrial systems
- Commercial and large energy-load systems
- Technical, economic, and environmental performance analysis
- Workforce and educational materials and activities related to energy systems

Research and Analysis

- Conduct literature reviews
- Collect and organize related technical, economic, and environmental data
- Compare and evaluate technology pathways using technical, economic, and environmental performance metrics
- Support spreadsheet analysis and technical documentation
- Summarize and present findings for researchers and project partners

Education and Curriculum Support

- Develop student-facing technical materials and case studies
- Prepare figures, presentations, and research summaries
- Adapt technical information for community-college audiences
- Support curriculum, workforce-development, and outreach activities

Work Arrangement

The internships will be fully remote, with regular virtual mentoring and team meetings. NLR will provide laptops and the required software and system access for remote work. No laboratory equipment or supplies will be required, as the work will focus on literature review, data analysis, spreadsheet-based analysis, and educational material development rather than laboratory experiments.

An optional visit to the NLR Golden Campus may be offered during the internship, subject to separate project funding, eligibility, scheduling, and NLR visitor requirements.

.

Basic Qualifications

Associate: Minimum of a 2.7 cumulative grade point average. Currently enrolled in an accredited associate degree program (community college or technical college) in a related field of study. Must be at least 18 years of age.

Undergraduate: Minimum of a 3.0 cumulative grade point average. Must be enrolled as a full-time student in a bachelor’s degree program from an accredited institution.

Post Undergraduate: Earned a bachelor’s degree within the past 12 months, with minimum of a 3.0 cumulative grade point average. Eligible for an internship period of up to one year.

Please Note:
• Applicants are responsible for uploading official or unofficial school transcripts, as part of the application process.
• If selected for position, a letter of recommendation will be required as part of the hiring process.
• Must meet educational requirements prior to employment start date

* Must meet educational requirements prior to employment start date.

Additional Required Qualifications

- Currently enrolled in an accredited associate or bachelor’s degree program in engineering, environmental science, chemistry, energy systems, data science, applied mathematics, economics, or a related field
- Interest in energy systems, sustainability, applied research, or technical education
- Basic proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint
- Strong written communication and organizational skills
- Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a remote environment
- Experience conducting literature reviews or organizing technical information
(Bachelor-level applicants only)

Preferred Qualifications

- Relevant coursework in engineering, science, statistics, economics, or energy systems
- Familiarity with spreadsheet analysis, data visualization, or technical documentation
- Experience preparing basic technical reports, presentations, or educational materials
- Interest in bio-based products, industrial systems, large energy-load systems, or workforce development
- Experience comparing technical, economic, or environmental performance metrics
(Bachelor-level applicants only)

.

Job Application Submission Window

The anticipated closing window for application submission is up to 30 days and may be extended as needed.

Annual Salary Range (based on full-time 40 hours per week)

Job Profile: Undergraduate / Annual Salary Range: $34,800 - $55,700

NLR takes into consideration a candidate’s education, training, and experience, expected quality and quantity of work, required travel (if any), external market and internal value, including seniority and merit systems, and internal pay alignment when determining the salary level for potential new employees. In compliance with the Colorado Equal Pay for Equal Work Act, a potential new employee’s salary history will not be used in compensation decisions.

Benefits Summary

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision insurance; 403(b) Employee Savings Plan with employer match*; and sick leave (where required by law). NLR employees may be eligible for, but are not guaranteed, performance-, merit-, and achievement- based awards that include a monetary component. Some positions may be eligible for relocation expense reimbursement. Internships projected to be less than 20 hours per week are not eligible for medical, dental, or vision benefits.

* Based on eligibility rules

Badging Requirement

NLR is subject to Department of Energy (DOE) access restrictions. All employees must also be able to obtain and maintain a federal Personal Identity Verification (PIV) card as required by Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12), which includes a favorable background investigation. Intern assignments extending beyond six months will be subject to this requirement.

Drug Free Workplace

NLR is committed to maintaining a drug-free workplace in accordance with the federal Drug-Free Workplace Act and complies with federal laws prohibiting the possession and use of illegal drugs. Under federal law, marijuana remains an illegal drug.

If you are offered employment at NLR, you must pass a pre-employment drug test prior to commencing employment. Unless prohibited by state or local law, the pre-employment drug test will include marijuana. If you test positive on the pre-employment drug test, your offer of employment may be withdrawn.

Submission Guidelines

Please note that in order to be considered an applicant for any position at NLR you must submit an application form for each position for which you believe you are qualified. Applications are not kept on file for future positions. Please include a cover letter and resume with each position application.

.

• Translate analytical results into clear visualizations, summaries, and user-friendly outputs for policymakers and other stakeholders.
• Collaborate with members of the Drive to Zero team and other CALSTART teams to prepare existing tools and resources for global adaptation and replication.
• Support other research and analytical activities related to zero-emission medium- and heavy-duty vehicles, infrastructure, and enabling policy as needed.

Intern Project Key Deliverables:

Toolkit for freight corridor electrification deployments

Qualifications:

• Current enrollment in, or recent completion of, a Master's degree in engineering, energy, transportation, environmental science, economics, data science, public policy, or a related field.
• Experience developing quantitative models, particularly TCO, techno-economic, financial, or policy-impact models.
• Familiarity with web-based tools, databases, dashboards, or digital knowledge platforms.
• Knowledge of zero emission medium- and heavy-duty vehicles, transportation electrification, charging infrastructure, or energy systems.
• Familiarity with clean transportation policies and the role of incentives, taxation, regulation, and other policy mechanisms in influencing vehicle economics.
• Experience translating analytical work into intuitive and user-friendly tools or visualizations.
• Interest in working in an international environment and supporting governments and other stakeholders in the transition to zero-emission transportation.

Immuta is the Data Authorization Company, helping the world’s largest organizations control who, and what, can access their data.

The way enterprises access data is fundamentally changing. Organizations are racing to put data to work across analytics and AI, while AI copilots and agents are emerging as an entirely new class of data consumer. Traditional approaches built around tickets, static permissions, and manual approvals were not designed for this speed, scale, or complexity.

Immuta provides the authorization layer for modern data and AI. Our platform enables organizations to provision governed access to data by policy, by request, and dynamically for AI agents, so people and AI can access the data they need while enterprises maintain security, compliance, and control.

For Chief Data Officers, that means making enterprise data dramatically easier to access and use without giving up governance. For AI leaders, it means giving AI agents secure, governed access to enterprise data so they can move from experimentation into production.

Founded in 2015, Immuta is trusted by Fortune 500 companies and government agencies worldwide.

- Our technology ecosystem includes Snowflake, Databricks, AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Okta, ServiceNow, Teradata, Alation, Atlan, and Starburst — connecting Immuta to the data, cloud, identity, and enterprise platforms powering modern data and AI environments.

- Immuta has been recognized by Forbes as a top American startup employer, by Inc. Magazine and Built In as one of the best workplaces, and by Fast Company as one of the world’s most innovative companies.

- Immuta has raised $263 million from investors including NightDragon, Snowflake, Databricks, ServiceNow, Citi Ventures, Dell Technologies Capital, DFJ Growth, IAG, Intel Capital, March Capital, Okta Ventures, StepStone, Ten Eleven Ventures, and Wipro Ventures.

- We operate as a hybrid workplace with offices in Boston, MA; Columbus, OH; and College Park, MD.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Product Engineering team builds and improves Immuta’s product, a platform that helps organizations use and govern access to data. The team works across software, data, and cloud technologies to turn product ideas and customer needs into reliable capabilities.

As a Product Engineering Intern, you’ll work alongside software engineers and other teammates to build, test, and improve the product. You’ll see how an idea becomes working software, how teams make technical decisions, and what it takes to ship and support code in production.

YOUR INTERNSHIP

At Immuta, interns are treated like members of the team. You’ll join the team’s regular workflow, contribute to real work, and take on responsibilities that reflect your skills and the team’s priorities.

The exact projects will depend on what the team is working on next summer, but you can expect to:

- Join the Product Engineering team as an engineer, rather than working on a separate intern-only project.

- Contribute to real product work that may be released to production.

- Apply concepts from your coursework to practical software engineering problems.

- Work with teammates to understand problems, explore solutions, build software, and improve existing product capabilities.

- Develop your skills through the team’s normal engineering workflow, including coding, testing, debugging, documentation, and collaboration.

- Take ownership of well-scoped work, communicate your progress, and ask questions when you need context or support.

- Learn how engineers build and maintain software that supports real customer needs.

TOOLS & TECHNOLOGIES

Depending on your role, you may work with:

- TypeScript

- Node.js

- Angular

- PostgreSQL

- Docker

- APIs, data platforms, and software services

- AI-enabled tools and workflows used by your team

You do not need to know every tool listed above. We’re looking for a strong foundation, curiosity, and the ability to learn.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

- A strong foundation in computer science or computer engineering, including experience with at least one programming language.

- Curiosity, initiative, and willingness to learn.

- Strong problem-solving, communication, and collaboration skills.

- Experience beyond coursework, such as an internship, hackathon, side project, or other extracurricular experience, is a plus.

Benefits

At Immuta, our goal is to help bridge the gap between personal and professional growth, so that our team members can be well and thrive personally and professionally. After all, great professional success stories rarely happen without great personal success stories! Our generous benefits package given to all full time employees includes:

- 100% employer paid Healthcare (Medical, Dental, Vision) premiums for you and your dependents (including Domestic Partners)

- Stock Options

- Paid parental leave (Both Maternity and Paternity)

- Unlimited Paid time off (U.S. based positions)

- Learning and Development Resources
